figure_verdicts.semantic_check: The three arrow groups are geometrically consistent with the caption's convention where they can be seen: the first two groups each pair one downward grey edge with one upward dashed red edge (a reversal that would close a cycle), and the third group has two edges leaving one upper node toward two lower points (the second live tip). Which names sit at those nodes, and which group is the fold, the refinement or the three history-apart cases, cannot be recovered from the render because no label is drawn.

findings.summary: The rendered image carries no text at all: 7,639 non-white pixels form 33 components, all of them grey arrow shafts and red dashes lying inside y 281-476, with rows 480-719 blank and no glyph-shaped component anywhere. Nothing names a node, a panel or an edge, so a reader sees three unexplained arrow groups and cannot tell the fold from the refinement or the branch case. Per the rubric this is a blocking defect - data the figure does not let a reader see - because the figcaption keys every identity (electron_density_at_plasma_boundary as the live tip, electron_density_at_pedestal_top as the proposed one) to names the picture never shows.

Two renders of the same repository path disagree. The reviewed run's figure-review.log records ImageMagick convert -density 140 to a 1714x882 PNG and reports that labels stay inside the canvas and do not overlap; the review attachment is a 1399x720 render of that path and contains no text whatsoever. Whatever a reader ends up seeing therefore depends on an unrecorded renderer choice, so the deliverable cannot be reproduced or checked by the next reader; the fragment embeds the SVG directly and should be checked in a browser before the figure is relied on.

rubric_lines: RUBRIC legibility: fail. The render carries no text of any kind. The whole non-white content is 7,639 pixels inside a 1117x196 band at +165+281, and the 33 ink components are exactly three grey arrow shafts with heads, two red dashed arrow lines with heads, and one red dashed diagonal - no glyph, no node label, no panel heading, no title and no axis. Rows 480-719 are entirely blank (interior probe y=520-600, x=200-1300 returns 0 non-white pixels; row 531 returns 0). The figcaption keys the figure to node names ('electron_density_at_plasma_boundary is already live', 'the proposed electron_density_at_pedestal_top'), so with no labels a reader cannot tell the three arrow groups apart or follow which pair is the fold, which the refinement and which the second-live-tip case.

RUBRIC data_ink: fail. No decorative ink is present, but 99.24% of the canvas is blank (7,639 of 1,007,280 pixels) and the ink that would carry the data - the node names the arrows connect - is absent, so the marks convey only direction and carry no identity. The arrows themselves are thin (2 px shafts, 4-8 px dashes) and read cleanly at native size.
RUBRIC decoration: pass. Transparent ground with no gradient, background fill, frame, gridline, drop shadow or styled theme; the only ink is grey #929292 and red #B42318 strokes.

RUBRIC contrast: fail, by absence rather than by level. No text is rendered, so 'text clears the contrast of its background' cannot be satisfied. The two colour families present are grey #929292 on white at 3.11:1 and red #B42318 on white at 6.57:1; both are antialiased to near-white only at their edges.

RUBRIC table_form: pass. A three-panel edge diagram with one stored and one refused edge per case is an adjacency a reader must see as a shape; the reviewed fragment carries the case disposition as a separate table, so the figure is not depicting tabular information.

RUBRIC label_collision: pass narrowly. Nothing is clipped - zero non-white pixels in each 3 px outer frame strip, with the same predicate returning 14, 11, 8 and 11 pixels on the first content rows, last content rows, first content columns and last content columns, so the zero is a measurement and not a dead probe - and no label overlaps another label or the data because the renderer drew no labels at all.
